thread.title: Indexes Hit Record Highs, Technology Sector Leads; Nvidia Hits Buy Point

author: JUAN CARLOS ARANCIBIA
title: Indexes Hit Record Highs, Technology Sector Leads; Nvidia Hits Buy Point
text:
The technology sector led a market higher Friday, as a number of tech leaders such as Nvidia ( NVDA ) broke out past proper buy points .
X The technology-rich Nasdaq composite climbed 0.8% and made a new all-time high. The S&P 500 rose 0.6% to also make a record high.
Small caps got in the act as the Russell 2000 added 0.4%. The index is firming up above the 1700 level. Not to be overshadowed, the Dow Jones industrial average rose 0.6%, but it is still 3% below its peak on Jan. 26.
Volume rose on the Nasdaq and fell on the NYSE compared with the same time Thursday. Advancers led decliners by 2-to-1 on the NYSE and by 8-to-5 on the Nasdaq.

Powell sounded dovish on interest rates as he called the U.S. economy "strong" and saw inflation contained. The chairman spoke at a gathering of monetary policy leaders in Jackson Hole, Wyo.
Cybersecurity, software, semiconductors and solar energy were among a broad group of leading sectors. The Philadelphia semiconductor index climbed 1.4%, adding a bit of room above its 50-day moving average.
Curiously, the largest tech companies were fairly quiet. Alphabet ( GOOGL ) rose 0.9%; Microsoft ( MSFT ), Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) and Apple ( AAPL ) were slightly higher; Facebook ( FB ) rose 0.7%. Intel ( INTC ) did better, up 1.5%.
Earnings from a few software companies seemed to spread to the rest of the technology sector.
Splunk ( SPLK ), a cybersecurity provider, roared 16% past the 121.74 buy point of a solid base . The company beat expectations for the July-ended quarter on a combination of favorable factors, including a new business model, and a rebound in international growth.
Autodesk ( ADSK ) gapped out of a base after Q2 earnings beat expectations . The relative strength line made a new high too — a good sign. The design software company's shares spent much of the 10-week basing period below the 50-day moving average. But today's move was the most bullish move since another post-earnings gap up on March 7.
Nvidia broke out of a flat base , clearing the 269.30 buy point in active trading. The leader in chip sets for video gaming, data centers, autonomous vehicles and other applications was volatile after its Aug. 16 earnings report but has recovered. Nvidia was added to Leaderboard after spending some days as an options play.
Arista Networks ( ANET ) rallied to a new high on news that the networking leader will be added to the S&P 500 index as of the open of trading on Tuesday. Arista touched the 311.77 buy point but traded below it in the afternoon.
